note: Responsive Table Filter ships one text-format filter, filter_responsive_table, that wraps <table> tags in a scrollable wrapper (figure by default) with tabindex=0 and aria-label='Scrollable table'. Settings wrapper_element (default figure) and wrapper_classes (default responsive-figure-table) are stored per text format at filter.format.<id> -> filters.filter_responsive_table.{status,settings}. No configure route, no permissions, no Drush. Medium/hard cases create a dedicated namespaced text format (rtf_*) and read/verify that filter's live config; cleanup deletes the throwaway format.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal contrib module Responsive Table Filter do to a <table> in rendered content, and what makes the table actually scroll on small screens? Mention the wrapper and the accessibility attributes it adds.
evals.expected_output: Its filter (filter_responsive_table) wraps each <table> in a wrapper element (a <figure> by default, class responsive-figure-table) with tabindex="0" and aria-label="Scrollable table". The attached CSS gives that wrapper max-width:100% and overflow-x:auto, which makes wide tables scroll horizontally.

evals.prompt: There is no settings page for Responsive Table Filter after I enabled the module. How do I actually turn it on, and what is the filter's plugin id?
evals.expected_output: It has no dedicated config page (configure=null). You enable the 'Responsive Table filter' (plugin id filter_responsive_table) per text format at Configuration > Content authoring > Text formats and editors (admin/config/content/formats).

evals.prompt: Which two settings does the Responsive Table Filter expose per text format, what are their defaults, and how would I change the wrapper from a figure to a div?
evals.expected_output: wrapper_element (default 'figure') and wrapper_classes (default 'responsive-figure-table'). Set wrapper_element to 'div' in the filter's settings on the text format (filters.filter_responsive_table.settings.wrapper_element).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, a text format named 'rtf_known' has the Responsive Table Filter enabled. Inspect the live configuration of that format and state which HTML element the filter wraps tables in (its wrapper_element setting).
evals.expected_output: The filter_responsive_table on filter.format.rtf_known has wrapper_element: section (and wrapper_classes: rtf-scroll-known).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the text format 'rtf_known' has the Responsive Table Filter enabled. Inspect the live configuration and state the CSS class(es) it puts on the wrapper element (its wrapper_classes setting).
evals.expected_output: The filter_responsive_table on filter.format.rtf_known has wrapper_classes: rtf-scroll-known (and wrapper_element: section).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a text format with machine name 'rtf_task'. Enable the Responsive Table Filter (filter_responsive_table) on that text format and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In filter.format.rtf_task, filters.filter_responsive_table.status is TRUE (e.g. tick 'Responsive Table filter' on the format at admin/config/content/formats/manage/rtf_task, or call FilterFormat::load('rtf_task')->setFilterConfig('filter_responsive_table', ['status' => TRUE])->save()).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the text format 'rtf_wrap' already wraps tables responsively using a <figure> element. Change it so the Responsive Table Filter wraps tables in a <div> element instead, and apply the change.
evals.expected_output: In filter.format.rtf_wrap, the filter_responsive_table is enabled and its settings.wrapper_element is 'div' (set the wrapper_element setting to div and save the format).
